title: The impact of patient-ventilator asynchrony in mechanically ventilated patients
author: Michihito Kyo
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bsqtndwn
materials: The impact of patient-ventilator asynchrony in adult mechanically ventilated patients on outcomes：A systematic review and meta-analysis (protocol) 2020/08/25 Department of Emergency and Critical Care Medicine, Graduate School of Biomedical and Health Sciences, Hiroshima University, Kasumi 1-2-3, Minami-ku, Hiroshima, 734-8551 Japan Michihito Kyo mkyo@hiroshima-u.ac.jp 1. Background Patients-ventilator asynchrony (PVA) is defined as a mismatch between the patient breathing efforts with a ventilator’s breath delivery. (1) PVA is a common problem in mechanically ventilated patients, (2, 3) which could potentially induce the exhaustion of diaphragm and respiratory muscles and deliver high tidal volume to the lung leading to ventilator-induced lung injury (VILI). (4, 5) The impact of PVA including an acute phase of mechanical ventilation on clinical outcomes was not similar across studies. Thille AW et al. reported that higher incidence of PVA was associated with longer duration of mechanical ventilation, while this was not associated with mortality. (2) Conversely, Blanch L et al. showed that ICU mortality of the patients with higher incidence of PVA was significantly higher than that with lower incidence of PVA. (6) Furthermore, to date, there is no systematic review regarding PVA in the acute phase of mechanical ventilation. Furthermore, although adjustment of sedatives or ventilator settings were thought to be effective for improving PVA, there is no definitive intervention for improving PVA without closed-loop-ventilation such as Neurally Adjusted Ventilatory Assist (NAVA) and Proportional Assist Ventilation (PAV) in the weaning phase of mechanical ventilation. (7, 8, 9) Therefore, we will conduct this systematic review and meta-analysis to clarify the impact of PVA on specific clinical outcomes and the effect of interventions in order to improve PVA for mechanically ventilated patients in the acute phase of mechanical ventilation. 2. Review question Part A. The impact of PVA on clinical outcomes To clarify the impact of patient-ventilator asynchrony in adult mechanically ventilated patients in acute phase of mechanical ventilation on outcomes. Part B. The impact of interventions for mechanically ventilated patients on PVA To clarify the impact of interventions for adult mechanically ventilated patients in acute phase of mechanical ventilation on PVA. 3. Method 3.1.1 Types of study to be included Part A. The impact of PVA on clinical outcomes

steps.title: Search for Relevant Studies
steps.instruction: Conduct a comprehensive search for published and unpublished observational studies and randomized controlled trials (RCTs), including crossover, cluster-randomized, and quasi-randomized trials.

substeps.instruction: Search the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), MEDLINE via Ovid, and EMBASE using the strategies in Appendices 1, 2, and 3.
Search the WHO International Clinical Trials Platform Search Portal (ICTRP) and ClinicalTrials.gov using strategies in Appendices 4 and 5.
Inspect references of extracted studies and the ATS/ESICM/SCCM international guideline on mechanical ventilation in adult patients with ARDS.

steps.title: Screen Titles and Abstracts
steps.instruction: Screen the identified titles and abstracts independently to determine study relevance.

substeps.instruction: Two authors independently screen titles and abstracts, discarding non-applicable studies.
Retain studies and reviews that may contain relevant data or trial information.
Contact study authors if necessary to assist in screening.
Two authors independently assess remaining abstracts (and full texts if needed) against inclusion/exclusion criteria.
Resolve differences in opinion through discussion or arbitration by a third author.

steps.title: Apply Inclusion and Exclusion Criteria
steps.instruction: Filter studies based on participant and intervention characteristics.

substeps.instruction: Include adults (≥18 years) in the acute phase of mechanical ventilation (within 72 hrs of initiation or when unable to trigger all breaths/using assist-control mode).
Exclude studies assessing NAVA or PAV interventions.
Exclude patients in weaning phase, post-operation, those with DNR orders, suspected bronchopleural fistula/air leaks, organ donation admissions, or pregnant patients.

steps.title: Extract Data
steps.instruction: Perform data extraction independently using standard forms.

substeps.instruction: Two authors independently extract data; resolve discrepancies via discussion or a third author.
Contact study authors if necessary for missing information.
Group multiple publications of the same study, using the most complete data version; highlight discrepancies between versions.

steps.title: Assess Risk of Bias
steps.instruction: Evaluate the risk of bias for included studies based on study design.

substeps.instruction: For Part A (PVA clinical outcomes), two researchers use the QUIPS tool to assess: Study Participation, Study Attrition, Prognostic Factor Measurement, Outcome Measurement, Study Confounding (Age, Severity score, Duration of MV), and Statistical Analysis and Reporting.
For Part B (Interventions), two researchers use the RoB 2 tool for randomized control studies.
For Part B (Interventions), two researchers use the ROBINS-I tool for observational studies.
Resolve disagreements via discussion or a third researcher.

steps.title: Perform Statistical Analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze data using STATA version 16 with random-effects models.

substeps.instruction: Calculate pooled odds ratios (ORs) with 95% CIs for dichotomous variables (mortality, reintubation, tracheostomy).
Calculate standardized mean differences or mean differences with 95% CIs for continuous outcomes (duration of MV in days, incidence of PVA in percentage).
Narratively summarize adverse events.
Handle missing values: Use intention-to-treat (ITT) for discrete variables; do not perform imputation for continuous variables.
Calculate standard deviation for missing values using the Altman method (if SE or p-values are reported) or Cochrane handbook/validated methods (if CIs and t-values are reported).
Assess heterogeneity using I2 (0-40% negligible, 30-60% mild-to-moderate, 50-90% moderate-to-substantial, 75-100% considerable). If I2 > 50%, conduct a χ2 test (p < 0.10 is significant).
Assess publication bias via trial registers; if >10 studies are included, perform funnel plot analysis and Egger's test (p < 0.05 is significant).

steps.title: Conduct Subgroup and Sensitivity Analyses
steps.instruction: Perform prespecified analyses to test the robustness of the primary outcomes.

substeps.instruction: Subgroup analysis by: ICU admission cause (Internal vs Traumatic), ARDS presence, Ventilator mode (Assist control/pressure support vs others), Timing (Acute phase vs Whole period), and PVA evaluation method (Human vs Software).

Sensitivity analysis by excluding: (i) studies using imputed statistics, (ii) studies without acute phase timing, (iii) post-operative patients, and (iv) high/moderate risk of bias studies (p < 0.05).

steps.title: Summarize Findings
steps.instruction: Create a summary-of-findings table using the GRADE approach to grade the certainty of evidence for all primary and secondary outcomes for both Part A and Part B.
